acceptance_criteria.source: Turn 4: "it's the right move to kick it up to the human in the loop for final adjudication, even if it means sharpening the definition or loosening it as needed, but it's a case by case basis, never assumed, never inferred, never projected from your end." acceptance_criteria.text: The project's written rules (CLAUDE.md) gain a rule stating that when a written spec or rule does not fit reality the human in the loop adjudicates, which may sharpen or loosen the definition, case by case, never assumed, inferred or projected by the agent.

acceptance_criteria.source: Turn 5: "playwright will make our adversarial reviews much tighter and more agressive now"; turn 6: "playwright gives the adversary better tooling to dig out those majors for us"; CLAUDE.md CARRIER rule: obligations cross rungs in documents, never by memory.

acceptance_criteria.source: Turn 7: "Code standard: every new addition to the code base, including new files needs to have a comment citing the ticket number."
acceptance_criteria.text: A code standard is recorded in the project's written rules (CLAUDE.md) requiring every new addition to the code base, including new files, to carry a comment citing its ticket number.

acceptance_criteria.source: Turn 8: "No, let's not backfill. Leave this as a demarkation line."
acceptance_criteria.text: The citation standard is recorded as forward-only: existing code is not backfilled, and the demarcation line from which it applies is stated.

acceptance_criteria.source: Turn 8: "This is a fossile for future bootstrapping. The fact that I only thought of codifying it now is the the class. The fix is to leave the scar there so everyone learns from it."
acceptance_criteria.text: The late codification of the citation standard is kept as a visible scar in the record, naming the lesson that the standard existed unwritten until now, so future readers learn from it.
